chapter: Owls, Werlein's and the OK record
title: School bands, Tulane dances and the theremin
summary: His band played fraternity dances; for Werlein's he organized school bands and demonstrated the theremin, including for Madame Schumann-Heink.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Oh, yes. Yes, sir. Sure. Why? Well, any place you go in New Orleans, you had a good band. But it looked like we played, the Owls or Brownlee's band would play for so many of the fraternities and sororities of Tulane. And then Loyola, of course, came into the picture after. And we played quite a bit up at Loyola Gym. We played up there very often. And I remember Cupera. You know, part of my work with Wuerline was organizing school bands. And that was my job was the Con Factory too, you see. For years I organized school bands. And then too, in my ability in music, there was an instrument came out that was invented by a Russian scientist, incidentally. The name was Theremin. And I used to demonstrate the Theremin in schools. In fact, I was supposed to go off with RCA people in demonstrating that. I demonstrated the Theremin to Madame Schumann-Heinck.

Yes. And that same day, I think Madame Schumann-Heinck gave an audition, as it was, to Marian Anderson, a colored woman, very fine voice, very fine person. And I used to play numbers like The Rosary and Because and numbers like that on the theremin. I guess old Johnny Hyman would remember that. Johnny, Johnny used to play around with it too, where it was Wuerlines.

Yes. And that was quite an instrument. I don't think that it lasted very long as a musical instrument to be sold in homes, but it was a fad. And it was to do. It was built on the basis of a radio chassis, and it had an upper vertical rod for your tones, and it had a parallel looped bar rod like for your expression with your left hand. And then you played it either with the point of a finger, or I played mine with the side and tip of my little finger. It was like that. And you knew the expressions were this way. And it had the voice of a cello and a violin. It was a very fine instrument.
